nonBlockingNotes: f1: feature-state.ts diff showed no changes (file was already clean of auto-injected flag in the reader). The spec pointed at src/infrastructure/feature-state.ts but the file lives at src/persistence/feature-state.ts. The normalizeFeatures function correctly drops unknown fields including auto-injected, so the migration goal is met even though the path in the spec was slightly stale.

f1: plan-service.ts drops `targets: [...feature.targets].sort()` from digestFeatures without a comment; this is harmless since targets is removed from FeatureDefinition, but a brief comment noting the removal would aid future readers.

f2: parseCommands keys are lowercased (line 64: key.trim().toLowerCase()) which is consistent and desirable. Authors writing 'Build: ...' will get 'build'. This is by design but not mentioned in the spec; worth documenting.

f2: formatCommandsInline uses '=' separator (key=value) while the charter.md source uses ':' (key: value). The test expects 'commands: build=bun run build'. This is intentional formatting for the status surface but is mildly surprising; non-blocking.

f3: The evidence-exists parser reads Kind: field into evidenceKind and FreshSince: into freshSince. Case-normalized via normalizeHeading so 'freshsince' matches 'FreshSince:' correctly. No test exercises evidence-exists parsing from charter.md text — spec only required the subagent parsing test. Non-blocking since VAL-VERIFIER-EVIDENCE-EXISTS is a schema criterion and the evidence-exists parse path mirrors the subagent path.
f3: SubagentVerifier and EvidenceExistsVerifier types are exported from verifier.ts and referenced in record-service.ts — clean separation, no god-file expansion.

Scope: record-service.ts gained ~340 lines (verifySubagentCriterion + verifyEvidenceExistsCriterion + helpers). This is the largest single-file growth. The functions are cohesive and in-scope for f3 (schema) + the dispatch features f4/f5. The dispatch implementations are likely landing here even though f4/f5 are separate features — acceptable since they are in the same milestone and tightly coupled.
